transcript.text: On the advance-notice obligation for those 2 enterprise tenants: customer success can handle this directly. I'll coordinate with the account managers to send formal written notice to both named tenants immediately after policy sign-off, documenting the service enablement date and the adjusted operating parameters. Given that next Monday is the planned enablement, we'd need to send that notice no later than end of this week to provide reasonable advance notice. If that timeline isn't sufficient, we may need to delay enablement for those 2 tenants specifically while proceeding with the broader rollout. As for other customer commitments — based on my reconciliation with account managers, only those 2 tenants have signed terms with specific replay and notice requirements. No other tenants have contractual obligations that the current policy would conflict with. On Marco's capacity finding: from a customer impact perspective, lowering to 60 rpm per tenant is workable, but I'd want to confirm none of our higher-volume webhook consumers would be affected before we finalize that change.

transcript.text: On whether 60 rpm and 3 replay workers are sufficient for production operations: based on my capacity findings this morning, those are the maximum values our reserved production capacity can actually support. I can't speak to whether that capacity is adequate for tenant demand beyond what the reservation allows; that's a question of whether we'd need to request additional reserved capacity if higher throughput is required. I haven't yet updated the policy ticket with these numbers, so I'd recommend we get the adjusted parameters formally recorded before sign-off.
